At the same time, hardware innovation cycles are compressing faster than before. Relying on traditional sequential handoff between design to manufacturing is no longer viable when customers expect rapid deployment. To compress our product maturity cycle to keep pace with surging manufacturing demand, we are restructuring how we team operating in the following ways.

First, we integrate pilot validation. We are embedding cross-functional teams of R&D engineers and manufacturing specialists directly into engineering pilot runs. By identifying thermal, mechanical, and assembly bottlenecks early, we can resolve issues in real time rather than waiting for post-production feedback loops.

Second, we have on-site supplier quality management. Rather than managing component quality remotely, we are forming a dedicated supplier quality engineering directly near our supplier sites. This hands-on oversight ensures tighter component tolerance, faster root cause analysis, and uninterrupted supply chain reliability as production scales.

By uniting R&D talent, localizing manufacturing, and proactive quality control under a core integrated framework, we are positioned to deliver reliable, high-density liquid-cooled infrastructure at the speed of market demand. Next page. The second topic is optics.

As generative AI cluster and hyperscaler data center scale continue to increase, traditional copper interconnects are rapidly approaching their physical limit in reach, power efficiency, and signal integrity. Transitioning from optical interconnect is no longer optional; it is essential to sustain high bandwidth, low latency infrastructure.

On the optics front, Accton strategy is built around three interconnecting pillar strategies: strategic component partnership, rapid parallel validation, and early stage manufacturing automation. The first pillar is to bridge optics ecosystem as a system vendor.

The photonics landscape is experiencing a surge of innovation, with numerous startups developing novel optical engines, switching fabrics, and interconnect architectures. As an open system networking system vendor, Accton sits in the critical interconnect between emerging component innovators and hyperscale data center operators.

Rather than looking into a single proprietary path, we maintain an open ecosystem-driven approach, actively partnering with optical companies whose roadmap aligns with our core architectural directions. For CPO and NPO, we all know CPO and NPO can bring optical engine closer to the switch ASIC and drastically shorten the electrical trace, lower power consumption per bit, and maximize front panel bandwidth density.

For OCS, enable dynamic optical network reconfiguration that eliminates unnecessary optical-electrical-optical conversions, reducing both latency and overall data center power budgets. For OWS, it's similar to OCS. OWS operates in different wavelength regions to carry more channels in a fiber for long-distance reach.

It is traditionally used for scale-up across use cases. However, we are looking into the feasibility to use it as a proven technology in scale-out use cases. The second pillar is to de-risk adoption through parallel technology test vehicles.

Breakthrough photonics companies often face steep hurdles when moving from a controlled lab environment into a thermally dense, high-volume switch system. To verify our parallel technologies are commercially and technically viable, Accton designs TTVs to help make decisions. Instead of evaluating optical technology sequentially, we run multiple TTVs in parallel across different architectures.
